hypothesis: A PID1-paid permanent one-online-stride-edit budget can limit repeated rewiring and lower compute in dense transient shocks, at the risk of leaving persistent drift unadapted and raising task probe costs. The first successful original paid PatchConst PC122 sets paid cell38 from 0 to 1. Every later failed probe pays to Read38 and, when the budget is exhausted, refrains from re-arming expensive success delta monitoring; F1 fallback remains enabled. Budget size one is intentionally severe and authored, not optimized using the new P4F5 holdout.
mechanism: After source-loaded F4 acquisition and paid PC82/131 PatchNext, PID1 follows original on-first-failure PC137. At PC137.next=142 it pays Const38, Read38, Sub(counter−1), Branch. If counter==1 it follows original PC140/141 F1 fail handler without re-arming success edge; if counter==0 it pays PC138/139 to arm F4 temporary success monitor PC106. A genuine post-failure success may compute online stride and pay PatchConst PC122, then F5 PC147..152 pays Read38, adds 1, Write38 and PC134..136 disarms the high-cost success monitor. Actor pays all arithmetic, source edits and memory operations. Counter bounds online PatchConst PC122 at exactly <=1 per world; earlier PC45/88/102 edits remain possible (not claimed bounded).
